thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Hosted gen-api (us-west-2) p99 latency > 2.5s for 6m; streaming stalls observed. Dashboard: https://dash.reedemo/alerts/9763 - paging oncall

maya (oncall): on it. seeing streaming stall alerts too. p95 jumped from 80ms -> 1.2s. p99 spikes to ~3s. impact: a subset of streaming responses are stalling mid-stream.

devin (infra): I can see a hot node in the shared gpu-pool-3: node-ugw-17. GPU util ~98% on GPU0, sustained PCIe write bursts, and iostat shows high sda5 avgq. suspected IO/GPU contention.

samir (ml-runtime): that pattern matches a noisy-tenant job thrashing KV cache and causing long tail for other sessions on same GPU (streaming stalls). Which tenant is on GPU0?

devin (infra): found pod: tenant-x/big-ml-job-0 PID 23456 pinned to GPU0. kubelet cgroup limits look like they did not apply properly on that node (missing device plugin restart).

lina (sre): immediate mitigation options: 1) evict the offending pod, 2) drain node so router moves new streams off it, 3) route new requests to fallback model variant until we stabilize. preferev quick evict then drain.

maya (oncall): agree. @devin can you evict and cordon node? keep me posted. I'll start customer impact assessment and notify CS.

devin (infra): doing eviction now. command:

```
kubectl delete pod big-ml-job-0 -n tenant-x --grace-period=0 --force
kubectl cordon node-ugw-17
kubectl drain node-ugw-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

devin (infra): also attaching nvidia-smi output just before kill:

```
GPU 0: 98% | Processes: 1: big-ml-job (PID 23456) | FB Memory  23.1G/24G
```

devin (infra): pod deleted; node cordoned; router should stop scheduling new streams to node-ugw-17. starting live-monitor for 10m.

samir (ml-runtime): redis KV cache hit-rate recovered from 46% -> 91% for the affected model prefix after eviction. streaming stalls count dropped to almost zero. tail latency (p99) back to ~220ms. good sign.

maya (oncall): customer impact: ~12k requests affected in last 6m; 3 customers >1% error rate or severe stall (tenant-x, tenant-y, tenant-z). Patrick can you start notifications for those customers with an initial brief?

patrick (customer-ops): prepping notifications. will send initial notific: short blurb + ETA for resolution. also flag enterprise customers for follow-up.

lina (sre): quick root-ish notes: cause = tenant-x long-running job bypassed gpu device quota enforcement due to device-plugin restart bug on node-ugw-17. secondary cause = high PCIe/io writes causing host-level IO wait affecting other containers.

maya (oncall): severity: P1-ish because SLO breach for hosted customers and streaming degraded; we mitigated by eviction/drain and p99 returned to acceptable band. moving to controlled state.

samir (ml-runtime): recommended followups (short):
- audit device-plugin restart behavior and add watchdog to reapply cgroup/device limits
- add per-tenant GPU reservation quotas and per-pool eviction thresholds
- alert on per-node GPU pci(e) bandwidth/IO latency spikes
- add router fallback policy: auto-fallback to smaller model variant when node-level contention detected

devin (infra): immediate infra tasks (short):
- repro on staging with device-plugin restart, confirm cgroup loss
- patch kubelet/device-plugin to reapply limits on restart
- create per-node IO alert (iostat avg-q > X)

maya (oncall): handoff: devin will lead postmortem and remediation tracking. I'll assign a follow-up ticket and schedule a blameless postmortem session.

patrick (customer-ops): sent initial notifications to affected customers. one replied asking for timeline and whether any data was lost — answer: no data lost, requests were delayed/streaming stalled only.

samir (ml-runtime): monitoring note: need to add a streaming-stall metric (streams with no frames > 1s) and tie it to tenant/node so we can quickly surface noisy neighbor cases.

lina (sre): adding a short-term mitigation runbook step: if per-node GPU util > 90% and p99 > threshold -> cordon node + evict long-running non-critical pods; router marks node as no-new-sessions for 10m.

maya (oncall): status: resolved -> mitigated. bringing this thread to incidents for postmortem. tagging next-oncall @devin to take lead. :thumbsup:

devin (infra): will take postmortem, create remediation ticket, and assign owners. thanks all.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to "mitigated" by maya (oncall).
